corrected_text: The number of sacral vertebrae is still more various, even in the species of the same genus. Thus, while in several of the ape genus, in the lori, in the vampyre bat, the colugo (galeopithecus), the coati, and two of the didelphis, there is one sacral vertebra only, most of the apes have sacra consisting of 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 pieces; the majority of other animals have 3 sacral vertebrae; the hedgehog, porcupine, guinea pig, paca, hare, tiger, several of the murine genus, the ant-eater, rhinoceros, camel, dromedary, chamois, goat, sheep, and ox, have 4; the elephant has 5; the Ai 6; the Unau 7; and in the mole, white bear, and quagga, they also amount to 7. The frequency of the three sacral vertebrae in the lower animals shows that Galen, who ascribes only 3 to the human subject, must have derived this inference from the former.
